item.title: Palace receive double fitness boost ahead of Hoffenheim clash
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Crystal Palace's Quinten Timber (L) and Middlesbrough's Adilson Malanda battle for the ball during the English Carabao Cup third round soccer match between Crystal Palace and Middlesbrough at Selhurst Park. (is associated with: «Palace receive double fitness boost ahead of Hoffenheim clash») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Crystal Palace have been boosted by the returns of Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen for the home match against Hoffenheim in the Europa League on Thursday. Midfielder Timber and striker Strand Larsen have been sidelined through injury since Palace’s last European outing, the 2-2 draw away at Besiktas on October 22. Boss Pierre Sage told a pre-match press conference: “Both will be back with us. “They were training with us last week but not ready to play, but now they are ready to play. All the others will be OK.” Palace will attempt to build on their tally of four points from their opening three league phase matches against the Bundesliga side. The showdown under the lights at Selhurst Park will be their eighth game in the space of 25 days, with the Eagles juggling their Premier League and League Cup commitments with Europe. Sage is eager to put their domestic issues to one side after Palace slipped to 18th following three straight defeats. He added: “First of all it’s exciting, because if we play in a European cup, it’s because the team did well last year and won the Conference League. We have to deal with that, but it’s a good thing. “To deal with three different competitions, for the process, it’s always the same because we prepare in the same way. “The difference between the three competitions is the time we have before the games to prepare. “This time we have three sessions before the game, one more than the two before, and that’s really important because we need time to work, especially when we’re in our situation. “What we did during these sessions was really important for the confidence of the players, for their understanding of the game plan and for their capacity to apply it.”

item.title: Cunha avoids sanction for not going straight down tunnel after red
item.description: Manchester United's Matheus Cunha leaves the pitch after being shown a red card during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Cunha avoids sanction for not going straight down tunnel after red») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Matheus Cunha will avoid UEFA punishment for failing to go straight to the dressing room following his late red card in Manchester United’s Champions League win against Roma. Michael Carrick’s Red Devils roared to a much-needed 3-2 comeback victory on Tuesday, when the Brazil international earned a penalty which was converted at the second attempt by Bruno Fernandes. Cunha equalized and then scored a dramatic late winner, with the United forward earning a booking having taken off his shirt in celebration and jumped into the Old Trafford crowd. A second yellow card soon followed for a poor challenge, with the ex-Wolves man then trying to watch the remainder of stoppage time before celebrating with team-mates, when rules state he should have left the field area. United boss Carrick pointed him towards the tunnel and UEFA has confirmed Cunha will serve just the one-match ban at Sporting Lisbon later this month rather than anything more severe. A spokesperson for the governing body said: “The UEFA official reports did not mention anything about this incident. “Therefore the automatic one-match ban following two yellow cards should not be extended for this reason. We are not investigating further this matter.” United livewire Cunha became the first player in Champions League history to win a penalty, score a goal and be sent off in the same match. Head coach Carrick said: “Matheus can do those things, he has those moments. “We put him inside, we swapped him with Bryan (Mbeumo) at half-time to try to get him in the middle of the pitch, to try to give us a little bit of a different shape, putting him in the centre of the pitch. “He found himself in good positions. Disappointed with how it finished but, again, it just shows how much he cares and he’s willing to do, when he’s in that frame of mind and he’s in that mood, that’s why we want him here.”

item.title: Lampard happy with increased output from Coventry’s summer signings
item.description: Lampard happy with increased output from Coventry’s summer signings Frank Lampard says he is pleased with the increased contributions shown by Coventry City’s summer signings. Coventry claimed their third win of the season last weekend against Sunderland , with five summer signings starting, having spent around £130 million on 12 new signings during the summer transfer window. The Sky Blues find themselves in 16th place in their Premier League after nine matches, two points and places above the relegation zone. Ahead of his side’s clash with Everton on Friday night, Lampard spoke of his delight at how his new players have integrated within the established players in the squad. Lampard said: “I would guess my selection so far was probably about three new players, sort of on average, and I think it’s an interesting point because I keep talking about it, but the players that came up [with us], we’re very, very happy with and some of them haven’t played in this league a lot, so they will be learning on their feet a bit. “When we recruited, we wanted to recruit players that could come in and help us, as in start for us, I really pushed to be there because we haven’t got time for development. You can’t get promoted and try and develop too much. “So I think it’s nice that in nine games you’re seeing that now, pretty even push of the new players coming in, understanding what we do, how we train, how we behave, what’s the demands of the team, and some get that quicker than others. “And the players here who live in their own individual cases have never maybe played in the Premier League striving to get there, we have to give them some time. “So I think to come to have five there, I’m not counting those numbers specifically, but I think when you put it that way, I think it’s interesting and it maybe shows that we’re hopefully getting a nice push from everyone to try and make the team.”

item.title: Wilder v Opetaia joins Fury vs Joshua undercard live on Netflix
item.description: Deontay Wilder will fight Jai Opetaia on the undercard for Tyson Fury ’s long-awaited fight with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff. The 31-year-old Opetaia, who is unbeaten in 31 bouts, winning 24 by knockout, will move up from cruiserweight to heavyweight against the former world champion Wilder. Jai Opetaia had previously called out the unbeaten David Benavidez (Getty) Wilder has history with Fury and lost the final two bouts of their trilogy, with the 41-year-old since returning to winning ways by beating Derek Chisora in London in April . Zuffa Boxing champion Opetaia had previously been linked with unbeaten three-weight world champion David Benavidez, although he will instead face Michael Cieslak . Opetaia had previously signed for Dana White ’s Zuffa Boxing, with White involved in the promotion of Fury-Joshua on 11 December. The former heavyweight champions will meet in a contest almost a decade in the making , headlining at Wales’s Principality Stadium and live on Netflix. Fury, 38, and Joshua, 37, are expected to make their ring walks in the early hours of Saturday morning, and now the support bouts have been announced for the Friday evening.

item.title: Gold postbox to honor Manx athlete
item.description: A postbox in Marown has been painted gold in honor of Manx athete Matthew Bostock [BBC] A postbox has been painted gold in celebration of a two-time gold-medalist athlete. Manx-born cyclist Matthew Bostock, from Marown, was crowned world champion in the 40km race at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in August, andwon Men's scratch race at the UCI Track Cycling World Championships in China last month. The idea to honor the 29-year-old with a gold postbox was put to the Isle of Man Post Office by Marown Commissioners. "Matthew is very humble, he doesn't go around shouting about his achievements. We wanted to do this for him, especially on Ballagarey Road, as that is where he grew up and his family lives," said commissioner Alison Lynch. Lynch said the idea came about following a similar accolodate for Peter Kennaugh in Onchan in 2012 following his world record-breaking achievement at the London Olympics. "Onchan requested for a postbox to be painted and they got it... so we spoke to Matthew's family first and got their consent before approaching the Post Office," Lynch said. Matthew Bostock took the final medal of the 2026 Commonwealth Games [BBC] She added that while Bostock and his family had not seen the box yet, his parents were "very proud, extremly happy and grateful" and Bostock was "absolutely over the moon". "He is hoping to be on the island towards the end of November, and we will try to get something arranged at the box," she added. Lynch said having watched Matthew grow up in the parish and reach the heights he had made her extremely proud. "Not just me, everyone on the Isle of Man is proud of his achievements. People wake up early to watch his live races no matter the time difference. He has a huge backing from here all cheering his on," she added. Bostock has been nominateed for the British Cycling National Champion of the Year award for 2026. The winner will be announced next week. item.title: Mirassol and Internacional win their matchweek 34 clashes
item.description: Mirassol and Internacional win their matchweek 34 clashes On Tuesday night (3), Internacional and Mirassol secured important results in the battle against relegation in the Brasileirão. Both teams won their matches, earning three points and some breathing room outside the bottom four. At Arena Condá, Mirassol beat Chapecoense 2-1. Kauan opened the scoring for the hosts just 12 minutes into the match, but Reinaldo and Shaylon completed the comeback for Mirassol. The win moved the team from São Paulo state into 12th place with 40 points and confirmed relegation for Chape, who sit bottom of the table with 21 points. Internacional defeated Coritiba 1-0 at Beira-Rio, with Alerrandro scoring in the 90th minute. The result put the team from Rio Grande do Sul outside the relegation zone overnight, but they need other results this round to go their way to stay out of the bottom four. Coritiba remain in 11th place with 42 points. In the opening match of the round on Monday (2), Red Bull Bragantino beat Santos 2-1, leapfrogging them in the standings. Rodinei's own goal and a strike from Wallace Yan gave Bragantino the win, while Philippe Coutinho scored for Santos. Matchweek 34 continues on Wednesday (4), with teams battling to secure top spot and others fighting relegation. At 7:30 p.m., Flamengo face Grêmio at the Maracanã, while Athletico-PR take on Vasco at Arena da Baixada. item.description: Ocon has driven in 198 grands prix since making his debut in 2016 [Getty Images] Esteban Ocon's career as a Formula 1 race driver is over - at least for the foreseeable future - after a falling-out with Haas led to the Frenchman being dropped for the rest of this season. Ocon, 30, was already going to be leaving Haas at the end of the year, with little prospect of finding a seat on the grid next season. But the acrimonious turn of events in Mexico City last weekend brought that forward by a few races. Ocon now faces a year on the sidelines, with the aim of finding a berth as a reserve driver, as he seeks to rebuild his career. This is not the first time he has found himself in this situation. Ocon was also without a seat in 2019 when he lost his drive at what had been called the Force India team after it was bought by Canadian billionaire Lawrence Stroll, who put his son Lance in Ocon's car. This, though, feels like it has more potential finality about it. Not least because 10 years into his career in F1, Ocon is well known within the sport, both his competitive level and his approach. He's been around the block a few times. His career has not been especially stellar. He has a reputation for falling out with teams and team-mates. And there is a new generation breaking through in F1, led by new world champion Kimi Antonelli. Ocon secured a rare podium finish in Brazil in 2024 for Alpine [Getty Images] Complaints and clashes with team-mates Haas had already run out of patience with Ocon long before Mexico City but whatever happened there was serious enough that Komatsu felt the relationship had to end on the spot. The decline of Ocon's time with Haas has echoes of previous experiences. Ocon has been beaten by team-mate Oliver Bearman over his two seasons at Haas, just as he was outpaced by Pierre Gasly and before him Fernando Alonso at Alpine, and Daniel Ricciardo before that when the team was known as Renault. When Haas signed Ocon, his reputation was such that many were surprised they had taken him. Komatsu felt he could make it work. But the team began to notice a pattern. When Ocon was struggling, he would become defensive and blame the team and car. Tensions would rise and the team felt there was a lack of accountability from the driver. There were also clashes with his team-mate, for example in Monaco practice when they got in each other's way and Bearman ended up calling Ocon "an idiot" over the radio. They also crashed into each other towards the end of the British Grand Prix last year. Competitive tensions between team-mates are common in F1. A driver's team-mate is also their biggest rival - the only person with the same equipment so the only driver against which they can be directly measured. The parallel need to work together to benefit the team's overall prospects can be an uncomfortable ask in such circumstances. It's a problem that is causing tension at Ferrari between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, for example, as was also seen in Mexico. But over the years, Ocon has built an unenviable reputation for both these sides of his character. To outsiders, this can be surprising because he is charm personified with the media, a delight to deal with. He and Gasly - who were childhood friends before falling out nearly 20 years ago - crashed twice together at Alpine. At the end of their two seasons together, was the first occasion on which Ocon was released before the end of the season, dropped with one race to go. Alonso and Ocon also fell out and the Spanish icon did not trouble to hide his distaste for his team-mate's behaviour at times. Ocon also had on-track clashes and team radio disputes with Sergio Perez when at Force India. Alpine also saw the same pattern as did Haas more recently in terms of self-awareness and accountability. Alonso put in a starring performance in wet qualifying in Canada in 2022 and stuck his midfield Alpine on the front row alongside Max Verstappen's Red Bull. That lap was 1.6 seconds faster than Ocon's and team insiders say he simply could not accept that he had been that much slower. item.title: Carlos Baleba injury: Michael Carrick says hamstring problem 'doesn't look great' for Manchester United
item.description: Carlos Baleba injury: Michael Carrick says hamstring problem 'doesn't look great' for Manchester United Michael Carrick has admitted Carlos Baleba 's hamstring injury 'doesn't look great' after the Manchester United midfielder was forced off in Tuesday's 3-2 win over Roma. Baleba pulled up clutching his hamstring just moments after the half-time restart at Old Trafford and appeared to be in tears as he made his way off. Carrick consoled the 22-year-old on the touchline. It is a cruel blow for United's £70million summer signing, who was only making his fifth start for the club. His debut had already been pushed back by an ankle problem he picked up during pre-season with Brighton. Baleba is almost certain to miss Sunday's Premier League visit of Aston Villa. He is also expected to remain at Carrington during the international break so United's medical staff can assess him further. The Cameroonian is set to miss his nation's Africa Cup of Nations qualification double-header with Namibia. Manchester United fears grow as Carrick says Carlos Baleba’s hamstring Injury ‘doesn’t look great’ Carrick stopped short of offering a timeline, but his tone after the game suggested United are bracing themselves for a lengthy absence. "I haven't got any more news on Carlos at this stage," said Carrick. "It's his hamstring, so we'll just have to assess what that looks like. Initially, it doesn't look great. Timelines, I haven't got much more to give you."

item.title: Why Brandon Aiyuk will likely be cut before he makes it to 49ers' facility Friday
item.description: Why Brandon Aiyuk will likely be cut before he makes it to 49ers' facility Friday originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There was some significant news recently regarding disgruntled San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk. He hired a new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, indicating that he's trying to make a comeback to the NFL. But it won't be easy for Aiyuk to return. He'll need to file for reinstatement from the Reserve/Left Squad list. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , that's exactly what Aiyuk just did on Wednesday. However, despite the news of Aiyuk's push to make an NFL return, with plans to return to the 49ers facility on Friday, the 49ers are likely to cut him before then. Why? Well, the team has made clear they have no plans to keep Aiyuk around. 49ers likely to cut Brandon Aiyuk after WR filed for reinstatement "Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has turned in paperwork to be reinstated, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus," Schefter reports. "Aiyuk, who is currently on San Francisco's Reserve/Left Squad list, will be reporting to the 49ers' training facility Friday afternoon, per Drew Rosenhaus." This is some significant news in the Aiyuk saga. For the first time since their split became evident last season, it appears likely Aiyuk will have a path forward in the NFL. But with the 49ers and Kyle Shanahan making it clear during the offseason that Aiyuk isn't in their plans, even with all of the injury issues at wide receiver, the 49ers are likely to cut him. The 49ers had two options with Aiyuk this offseason: trade him to an interested team, or cut him. But since he didn't file for reinstatement, the 49ers didn't have to do anything this whole time. MORE : Jayden Daniels snaps unbelievable drought with Commanders' win over Eagles Now, with Aiyuk trying to make an NFL comeback, the 49ers will, almost guaranteed, release the veteran WR. No team, even the Washington Commanders , where Aiyuk likely wants to go, will be willing to trade for him. There is far too much uncertainty about his abilities right now for a team to chance it with a trade. Not to mention the contract situation that no team wants to be a part of. Fans should expect the 49ers to cut Aiyuk soon, potentially before he even gets a chance to return to the 49ers' training facility. His time with San Francisco is over, even as he tries to make an NFL comeback halfway through the 2026 season. Aiyuk is likely to be cut by the 49ers, as his file for reinstatement will finally move things along with his NFL career. item.description: RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 27: The Carolina Hurricanes celebrate their 2-1 victory over the Boston Bruins at Lenovo Center on October 27, 2026 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Carolina Hurricanes struggled through a rare bad outing on Tuesday night against the Predators. But they are still rocking and rolling. Even the best teams will put up forgettable performances. That was the case when the Hurricanes skated into Nashville and lost 4-1 to the Predators. It wasn’t for a lack of effort; the Hurricanes put up 30 shots on goal compared to Nashville’s 20. Carolina has continued a trend that has lasted all season: After 17 games, they remain first in the NHL in average shots for and against per game. Per EdgeHalla, the Hurricanes are edging out the second-place New Jersey Devils with 32.9 shots for compared to Jersey’s 32.7. Carolina’s willingness to take shots at the net is one reason they rank third in the NHL with 64 goals scored. That is good for 3.76 goals per game. The Hurricanes are also edging out the Dallas Stars in shots against per game for the league lead. Dallas has allowed 22.5 shots per contest, while Carolina has allowed 22.3. Allowing just 20 against Nashville on Tuesday night surely helped the cause. Carolina’s Incredible Shots For vs. Shots Against Ratio Has Paid Dividends It is still early in the season, but this trend continues what drove the Hurricanes to hoisting the Stanley Cup in June. Across 82 games, Carolina finished second in the league behind only the Colorado Avalanche with 2,637 shots for, or 32.1 shots per game. Their 1,962 shots against was the lowest in the NHL. That translates to 23.93 shots allowed per contest. The Hurricanes were the only team in the NHL to allow under 2,000 shots. The Vegas Golden Knights came close, but they allowed approximately 2,000 shots. This isn’t to say Carolina will repeat as Stanley Cup Champions because of their shots-for-vs. shots-against ratio. That would be far-fetched so early in the season. But it shows just how effective the Hurricanes are when they take frequent shots at the net and allow so few of them. But that doesn’t mean the Hurricanes need to reinvent the wheel after one bad outing. Carolina’s willingness to take shots at the net is one reason they rank third in the NHL with 64 goals scored. That is good for 3.76 goals per game. The Hurricanes are also edging out the Dallas Stars in shots against per game for the league lead. Dallas has allowed 22.5 shots per contest, while Carolina has allowed 22.3. Allowing just 20 against Nashville on Tuesday night surely helped the cause. Carolina’s Incredible Shots For vs. Shots Against Ratio Has Paid Dividends It is still early in the season, but this trend continues what drove the Hurricanes to hoisting the Stanley Cup in June. That translates to 23.93 shots allowed per contest. The Hurricanes were the only team in the NHL to allow under 2,000 shots. The Vegas Golden Knights came close, but they allowed approximately 2,000 shots. This isn’t to say Carolina will repeat as Stanley Cup Champions because of their shots-for-vs. shots-against ratio. That would be far-fetched so early in the season. But it shows just how effective the Hurricanes are when they take frequent shots at the net and allow so few of them. This is also a team that found a way to lose against the rebuilding Calgary Flames before it went on to win five of its next six games, losing only in a shootout against the mighty Edmonton Oilers . The Hurricanes also posted shutout wins against the St. Louis Blues and Winnipeg Jets in that span. If there are two things the Hurricanes can’t do, it’s to play down to their competition. They face a solid New York Islanders team before squaring off with the Chicago Blackhawks and a double-header in Finland against the Seattle Kraken . None of the above match the Hurricanes. Given Carolina’s ability to overwhelm opponents with their high-octane approach while stopping scoring chances, they have an outstanding chance to rebound. item.title: Palmer should have been sent off for Fernandes barge - panel
item.description: Cole Palmer would have been suspended for three matches had he received a straight red card [Getty Images] Cole Palmer should have received a straight red card for violent conduct in Chelsea's 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur, the Premier League Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has ruled. The England international was cautioned by referee Chris Kavanagh in the 70th minute after barging into Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes. Palmer did so with such force that it caused the Portugal international's head to snap back. The KMI Panel voted 3:2 that Kavanagh should have shown a red card on the field. However, the KMI Panel unanimously supported the decision of the VAR, John Brooks, not to intervene. The majority of the five members of the KMI Panel felt it was "clear contact to the head as well as unnecessary, dangerous and made with excessive force". Two panellists viewed the action as "aggressive with no excessive force", supporting the booking. Palmer was sent off for a second yellow card in the 80th minute for a foul on Jan Paul van Hecke, which the KMI Panel supported 4:1. The midfielder received a one-match ban for his dismissal, missing the Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool. Had he been sent off for violent conduct, he would also have been suspended for Saturday's 2-0 victory over Manchester United, in which he scored a penalty, and this weekend's trip to Sunderland.

But even if Fahey improves as a passer with every successive game in November, he's got a long way to go to replicate Sayin's production and his connection on the field with Smith. And that gap between quarterbacks could ultimately decide how relevant Smith is in the Heisman discussion as we reach November. Ruiz does not have any guaranteed money on his deal after season. Green Bay Packers could trade for New Orleans Saints Right Guard Cesar Ruiz at the NFL trade deadline Getty The Rams could bolster the offensive line with a trade Ruiz is a former first-round pick, going 21st overall by the New Orleans Saints in 2020. Ruiz started in 9 games in his rookie season but has been a primary starter ever since. In his career, he has 89 career starts in his 7 years in the NFL. Overall, he has 5,942 career snaps, with 5,550 of them coming at right guard. He also has 378 snaps at center and 14 snaps at right tackle. Ruiz signed a four -year, $44 million extension with the New Orleans Saints in 2023. While he is signed through the 2027 season, the team acquiring him could release him after the season and not take on any dead cap. The New Orleans Saints are sitting at 2-5 at the bye week, and they could be looking to move on from their longtime right guard for a strong trade offer. Given the Packers’ need at right guard, they could be a fit for Ruiz. Packers Have Big Hole at Right Guard Green Bay was expected to start Anthony Belton at right guard, but he had to shift out to right tackle when Zach Bako-Bewele got injured in Week 2. The team started Jacob Monk for the first three weeks of the season, but Monk ended up getting hurt. After that, they moved to former tackle Travis Glover for the next couple of starts. Glover got hurt, but starting left guard Aaron Banks returned to the lineup, so the team moved left guard Laken Tomlinson over to the right side. The issue is that Laken Tomlinson is a 12-year player in the NFL with just one start in his NFL career at right guard, going back to 2016. His first start in ten years was up and down, but the team was able to get the win. Still, it is hard to think they can continue to lean on Tomlinson. The only case against adding Ruiz would be continuity. If the Saints are listening, Green Bay has to be offering. item.title: Leclerc to miss Brazilian GP media duties after daughter’s birth
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Monegasque Formula One driver Charles Leclerc of team Ferrari speaks to the media at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, ahead of the Mexican Formula One Grand Prix on Sunday. (is associated with: «Leclerc to miss Brazilian GP media duties after daughter’s birth») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc will miss media duties ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix following the birth of his first child. The Monégasque driver announced on Instagram that his wife Alexandra gave birth to their daughter Bianca on Tuesday. Leclerc had been scheduled to answer questions from the press on Thursday but has been allowed extra time at home with his family in Monaco. The 29-year-old’s absence means he will not address criticism from team-mate Lewis Hamilton following their tussle in the Mexico Grand Prix last weekend. Hamilton accused Leclerc of working against him after he tried to overtake the British driver during the first lap when the pair were in front, opening the door for Max Verstappen to win the race. “We have to have some serious talks behind the scenes for sure,” said Hamilton. “We don’t have rules of engagement and, whether or not that will change anything from Charles’ side, I don’t know. Something needs to change for sure. “I think it’s a mentality thing. It’s like, ‘Do or die. Either I win or none of us do’, and it shouldn’t be that.” The spat was met with frustration by Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur, who told Sky Sports: “I think it’s just a matter of respect. Honestly, it’s difficult to digest for me to give up a win like this.”

item.title: Zverev debuts as world number one with Paris Masters exit
item.description: German tennis player Alexander Zverev in action agaisnt Italy's Lorenzo Musetti during their their men's singles round of 32 match of the Paris Masters tennis tournament at Plenitude Arena. (is associated with: «Zverev debuts as world number one with Paris Masters exit») Matthieu Mirville/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa Alexander Zverev made his debut as men's world number one with a defeat to Lorenzo Musetti in the second round of the Paris Masters on Wednesday. The German is out of the tournament after a 6-7 (5-7), 2-6 defeat, while Musetti advanced to the third round. Zverev was competing for the first time since taking over the number one spot in the ATP rankings from Jannik Sinner. He will still finish the year at the top position. "It's pretty shocking the level I was able to play in front of Sascha, who was serving really well, especially in the first set," Musetti said in his on-court interview. Zverev was set to take control when he led 5-2 in the first-set tie-break. But Musetti raised his level and reeled off five consecutive points to snatch the opening set. "It was really close. It could have gone both ways. The key was to stay there at 5-2. I played five great points in a row," Musetti said.

item.title: You voted for the Brewers postseason MVP, and it was a landslide
item.description: Election night brought its share of one-sided results , and that was likewise true when we asked readers to tell us which Brewers player deserved the MVP of the entire run to a World Series championship. With more than 450 votes by the morning of Nov. 4, the clear-cut winner was Aaron Ashby. The relief pitcher garnered 230 of the 456 votes (50.4%), which is a pretty healthy chunk of the vote among nine possible choices. Ashby did something no pitcher has ever done in an MLB postseason before, working 18 relief innings without allowing a single run. Hall of Famer Goose Gossage, whose 1981 Yankees defeated the Milwaukee Brewers en route to an American League pennant, had the previous best relief-pitcher postseason in allowing zero runs over 14⅓ innings. Gossage was on the hill in the eighth inning of ALDS Game 5, when Don Money hit a fly ball that could have given the Brewers a 6-5 lead, but it died on the warning track and was caught by Dave Winfield. The Yankees added two insurance runs in their half of the eighth, and Gossage worked a 1-2-3 ninth in the 7-3 Yankees win. Andrew Miller of Cleveland recorded 16 straight scoreless innings in the 2016 postseason before allowing a home run to Dexter Fowler of the Cubs in Game 4 of the World Series. He ultimately allowed three earned runs in 19⅓ innings. The 28-year-old Ashby twice worked three innings in a postseason game and recorded more than three outs in every other one of his nine playoff appearances save for one. He allowed five hits and three walks but struck out 20 batters. He recorded the final nine outs against the Dodgers in Game 4 of the NLCS , stranding runners at third base with one out on two occasions, to send the Brewers to their first World Series since 1982. In the World Series, he worked 5⅔ innings and allowed just one hit with no walks and nine strikeouts. Ironically, Ashby had struggled in his previous postseason experience, allowing 16 hits, 10 walks and eight earned urns in 9⅓ innings. He had 10 strikeouts. His 30 postseason strikeouts rank fourth in Brewers history behind three other players encountered along the way in the 2026 playoffs: Freddy Peralta (41), Brandon Woodruff (also 41) and Jacob Misiorowski (32). The only other person close to Ashby in votes was catcher William Contreras, the World Series MVP who got 150 (33%). item.title: Mainoo and Lacey raise the spirits but systemic change still required at Manchester United | Nick Ames
item.description: There were protests at Old Trafford and even though two academy products stood out, Michael Carrick’s future is far from safe Green and yellow balloons bobbed around the Stretford End. Tennis balls rained down on the pitch in protest at the chronic, enduringly cinematic decline presided over by Manchester United’s ownership. Then came a reminder of the humble football’s extraordinary power to bend history, minds and wills. United’s players departed victorious having somehow won the game within the game, separating themselves from the fog of unhappy context swirling on all sides and turning the second half into its own soaring, ripping story for the ages. Will it be enough to save Michael Carrick, who was once again serenaded when minds wandered from the joint scourges of the Glazer family and Jim Ratcliffe? If Aston Villa defend a shade more competently than Roma on Sunday then perhaps not. United have led their supporters, remarkable in their tenor of backing for players and head coach here, up more than enough false peaks over the past 13 years. Arguably, that is one reason for Carrick being given the job on a permanent basis. Continue reading...

item.title: Lennart Karl steals in behind Atlético Madrid to inspire Bayern Munich win
item.description: “This stadium brings back bad memories but I hope to be able to replace them with good ones,” Harry Kane had said on Monday night, and 24 hours later this was a start. A small step, perhaps, towards coming back on 5 June and having a second go at winning the Champions League in the arena where he lost the 2019 final . On his first European outing since winning the Ballon d’Or , the England captain was unable to score but he and his Bayern Munich team defeated Atlético Madrid, fellow semi-finalists from last season. They did so in a way that suggests that their candidacy this season is serious. It may not have been sparkling but they had been superior almost from the start, dominant in physique and football. This is a team with few weaknesses, intense and impressive throughout. All Atlético could do was resist and it never truly felt like they would be able to do that for ninety minutes; ultimately, they lasted 54. That was when Lennart Karl scored the first. The superb Konrad Laimer then added the second on a night when they racked up nineteen shots. It had been heavy going for a while, and they had been made to wait, but in the end Bayern were just that bit too good. Continue reading...

While Football Daily hasn’t actually seen much of West Ham this season, we’ve noted enough of their results to presume they were doing OK in their attempt to bounce back to the Premier League after relegation. Less than a third of the way through the Championship season under Nuno Espírito Santo, they’d already spanked six without reply past both Wrexham and Lincoln, while scoring three or more in wins over Wolves, Derby and Bolton. However, it turns out that of the 13 matches they’ve played in a league that is famously difficult to get out of (unless you were Sheffield Wednesday last season ), they have actually lost three times and currently sit in eighth place, a whopping six points off leaders Middlesbrough. Given the context of such an unbridgeable chasm, it is small wonder West Ham fans woke up to news that Nuno had been unceremoniously bounced out of the London Stadium with a P45 in hand. While my heart aches for Jesús de Miguel, who has died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, I shudder to think the trauma that shall haunt Owono for the rest of his life. I do hope and pray the wider community understands and extends their support in his recuperation” – Krishna Moorthy. If the bit comes off, it is a shirt pull and the offender has the honour of putting it back in place before being awarded a yellow card” – Mike Harold. The problem with today’s highly paid professionals is that they simply have no panache at all when they go down. I recall watching Francis Lee pick up the ball on the halfway line at a mud soaked Maine Road in the late 1960s, he put his head down and headed for goal, he was determined, he was single minded. He was 30 yards from goal, he was in full flow. He was tackled from behind and then he really took off, he grew wings, he soared. I swear he landed in the penalty area over 10 yards away. He dragged himself to his feet and without a semblance of a smile smashed the well-deserved penalty, with a very heavy leather ball straight at the centre of the goal at over 70 mph. The goalkeeper, obviously no fool, simply dived out of the way. The press christened him “Lee Won Pen” He was my hero. That man had panache, he had style” – Myles Flynn. item.title: Arsenal have everything they need to repeat as Premier League champions | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Sunday’s win at Liverpool showed the Gunners are deeper, more experienced, and are playing against a weaker class of contenders than last season Sign up for our free newsletter here Arsenal are three points clear at the top of the Premier League table . But given the team in second are Manchester City, who are likely to be facing at the very least a major points deduction , perhaps more significant is that they are five clear of Brighton in third. The season of domination that many anticipated from the champions appears to be coming to pass. Liverpool challenged them on Sunday. There was a 20-minute spell before half-time when they swarmed all over Arsenal, and Anfield felt at least like it did in the golden years of Jürgen Klopp, when it buzzed with an energy that could overwhelm visitors. But Arsenal got through that, reset at half-time, and navigated the second half with relative comfort. For the second league game running, they denied Liverpool a shot on target. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Unai Simón caps myth-making week with another extraordinary night | Sid Lowe
item.description: Athletic’s win over Real Sociedad was culmination of six unique days for the Spain keeper after night at the Palladium For the third time in six days everyone got to their feet to hand a standing ovation to Unai Simón, dressed in all black, before the world. Named the best men’s goalkeeper on the planet, holding the Lev Yashin trophy, they had applauded him at the London Palladium on Monday night and before the game began at San Mamés, Bilbao, on Sunday. Now somewhere in the middle of it all, the ferocity of the 197th Basque derby, there was another moment, even more meaningful and more lasting, a cheer again giving way to something deeper: an appreciation for a man as well as his work closing a week that will be forever his. Which means it will be forever theirs too. Real Sociedad and Athletic Club had been doing battle for 72 minutes and it was 2-1 when Simon took off to make a save that denied Carlos Soler an equaliser and defied belief . As the ball flew off his palm, San Mamés exploded. And then it happened: never mind that Athletic still had a derby to win and a corner to defend, forget the fact that the lead was a single goal, the visitors relentless now and 25 minutes still to resist; at the stadium everyone calls the Cathedral , a place of ritual and liturgy like no other, the entire congregation, 50,092 people, started clapping. Started and did not stop. For a minute, maybe more, it was like the match that matters most didn’t matter at all, momentarily fading until it was just him and them together. Continue reading...

item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can support In Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Holloway at his finest. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
